tests.proves: L-1: every value that survives an authentication hop and then becomes a redirect is narrowed to this origin by ONE shipped helper, src/lib/tujuan.ts, which is IMPORTED AND EXECUTED here rather than read as text. Eleven legitimate destinations pass through with their query and fragment intact; twenty-four off-origin shapes are replaced by the caller's fallback -- the network-path //evil.example and its triple- and quadruple-slash forms, both backslash spellings a browser treats as slashes, the same three with a TAB, CR or LF in front (which the URL parser DELETES before parsing, so a check that reads the raw string is looking at a different string), userinfo and encoded-traversal variants, absolute http/https, javascript:, data:, vbscript: and file:. Each refusal is independently confirmed adversarial: the raw form is resolved by the same URL parser NextResponse.redirect will use and required to leave the origin, so a case that proves nothing cannot sit in the matrix unnoticed. THE PLANT RUNS IN-PROCESS: the startsWith('/') predicate this repair replaced is applied to the same matrix and must be shown to ACCEPT destinations that escape, so the test discriminates between the repair and the defect rather than passing against either. Also asserts the caller's fallback is honoured on refusal and NOT applied to a legitimate path, that a missing destination falls back, and that narrowing is idempotent -- what comes out is already the parser's own form, so a second parse downstream cannot read it differently from the parse that approved it

L-1 closure: the four sites that carry a destination across an authentication or action hop -- src/app/auth/callback/route.ts, src/app/masuk/actions.ts, src/app/masuk/page.tsx and src/app/belajar/actions.ts -- each narrow it through tujuanInternal, and none of them still decides with a bare leading-slash test, which is what all four did before. A comment-stripped walk over every .ts/.tsx file under src/ asserts that no OTHER file narrows a destination its own way, so a fifth site cannot be added outside the contract. The helper itself is required to RESOLVE the destination and compare origins rather than pattern-match, because replacing one leading-slash test with a longer list of forbidden prefixes would be the same defect with more lines

L-2: PINTAR 4.0 is institution-provisioned, so magic-link authentication proves access to an identity a school already created and does not create one. The signInWithOtp call carries shouldCreateUser: false -- the Supabase default is TRUE, so the flag's absence was the defect: an unknown address became an auth.users row, and on_auth_user_created then gave it a persons row and an accounts row. No signUp, admin.createUser or inviteUserByEmail call exists in the sign-in actions. AND THE PRIVACY HALF, which is the easy one to get wrong: with creation off an unknown address errors where a known one succeeds, so returning that difference would replace a self-provisioning defect with an account-existence oracle -- the refusal meaning 'no such provisioned identity' is therefore folded into the ordinary outcome and matched on a stable error code, and the actions are asserted to run no database pre-check against accounts or persons and no auth.admin lookup, either of which would rebuild the same oracle one round-trip earlier. The classroom-card path is asserted untouched: still signInWithPassword over deriveCardSecret, with no signup behaviour, so the human PIN has not become an account password

L-2 measured rather than configured: this EXECUTES against the running Auth service and the live schema rather than reading a flag. An address nobody has provisioned asks for a sign-in link exactly as the application asks (create_user: false, the wire form of shouldCreateUser: false), and creates nothing: no auth identity, no PINTAR person, no PINTAR account. Counted BEFORE and AFTER against the live schema, both for that address and as whole-table totals over auth.users, persons and accounts, so the proof is the pair rather than an absence that was always true -- and it is additionally required to have been refused BY THE PROVISIONING GATE, so a broken Auth service that also happens to create nothing cannot pass. The chain being protected is demonstrated in the same run as the plant: an auth.users insert still produces exactly one person and one account through on_auth_user_created -- planted inside a transaction and rolled back rather than exercised against the Auth service, because persons_no_delete means a row created for real could never be removed again, and the test asserts it left no residue. POSITIVE CONTROL, and it asks which gate refused rather than whether mail was delivered: a seeded provisioned address must NOT meet the provisioning gate, and the two addresses must meet different outcomes at it. Delivery is deliberately not asserted -- CI starts the stack with mailpit excluded, so there is no SMTP sink and the send step 500s for any address that reaches it, which is only the provisioned one; an earlier version asserted status < 400 and reported 'the contract refuses everyone' when the contract had let the address through and the runner simply had nowhere to post a letter

tests.proves: No file under src, selftest, supabase or scripts carries a literal control byte outside tab, newline and carriage return -- read as BYTES from the source tree rather than as text. This exists because this patch introduced exactly that defect and the suite went green anyway: src/lib/tujuan.ts, the L-1 destination helper, was written with a NUL, a 0x1F and a 0x7F spelled as real bytes inside the very character class that exists to refuse them. The regex still functioned, every behavioural case in L1-TUJUAN-01 still passed, and the only symptom was that git classified a security-critical source file as binary and would not diff it -- so the helper had become unreviewable while reading green. A byte a reviewer cannot see is not reviewed, and a test that exercises behaviour cannot detect it, so this one inspects the file contents directly

No file on the learning surface reads display_role, reads the role table, or names STUDENT, so nobody is being made one, and none of them moves a reader through an account boundary to reach their own learning. The shell offers two places to be, both of them real routes, and carries no control that changes a role, an account or a mode. And no file under src names learning_context, PROFESSIONAL_DEVELOPMENT, the academic evidence boundary or the scoped session source: provenance is the database's business and reaches no screen

No telling on this surface names teaching effectiveness, a performance score, a ranking or league position, a comparison with other educators, an appraisal, a promotion or a sanction, or a good or bad teacher -- watched on two plants, because a sweep that matches nothing must not be mistaken for a surface that says nothing wrong. AND THE EMPTY STATE IS AN ORDINARY STATE OF AFFAIRS: it is the same 'belum ada' construction the rest of the product uses, and in neither language does it name a fault, a refusal, a permission, an administrator to contact, a setting to change, or an account to go and get -- watched on a plant that points the reader at the wrong kind of account. W8-01, restated for BOB-08 (a): an institution administrator signed in builds a Bagian, a Tingkat and a Kelas in their own school through BOB-01's structure functions, and the Kelas carries a jalur 6 deep; the same administrator's direct writes to org_nodes and academic_periods are refused (42501); the ladder still refuses a step that is not a step, even to the owner; a dean, an educator and the neighbouring school's administrator are refused. Read from the migration source 20261012100000, which closes the direct write path.

The standing assertion behind W8-01: no table a client may write runs an invoker-rights trigger that calls a function the client cannot execute. It is checked for NON-VACUITY -- the sweep must cover real client-writable tables and real invoker triggers, because an assertion over an empty population is green and says nothing -- and it is owner-run, since a client-executable assertion about client executability would be answering about itself.

An institution assembles a reusable report template from PINTAR's live catalogue and generate_report runs on it. Before WP8 the catalogue, the tables, the capability, the guards and the engine all existed and report_templates held zero rows in every environment, because no product path could write one. The order given is the order kept; each generated entry carries the status the evaluator decided, so authorization still filters per metric; revising makes a new template VERSION rather than an edit in place, and a report already issued still names the version that produced it. The act is audited, and the audit row carries no figure.

The catalogue is PINTAR's and a template only selects from it. A metric of the school's own invention, a visualization the catalogue does not permit for that metric, a template that shows nothing, one that shows thirteen, one assembled for the neighbouring school, and a direct edit of a metric definition are each refused. An institution decides which metrics appear and how they are drawn; it cannot reach what they mean, how they are computed, who may read them or what the minimum sample is.

Authorization is the FIRST gate on the new endpoint, which is RF-2's lesson applied where it is cheap to apply. A dean, an educator and another school's administrator are refused by the capability's name -- and refused by the SAME name when the rest of the call could not possibly resolve: a null metric list, an invented standard report and a template id that does not exist. So the refusal proves authorization rather than a lookup that failed. An anonymous caller is refused too.

Two bounded corrections. A metric retired by a new catalogue version is refused at the moment a template selects it, while a template that named it before the retirement keeps its row -- a catalogue decision does not silently rewrite what a school assembled. And drawable_items_for_definition is no longer granted to a client that could never have used it: it is invoker-rights by design and calls an owner-only function, so a client call could only ever have failed. The assembler still reaches it and a seeded definition still draws its items, so delivery is intact.

A freshly deployed PINTAR can acquire its FIRST administrator, and no second one. Until the release rehearsal nothing could: INV-16 requires an authenticated grantor, forbids self-grant, and lets only an active SYSTEM_ADMIN grant SYSTEM_ADMIN, so an empty database had no door at all. The door added is the operator's alone -- a signed-in session and an anonymous one cannot reach it, by grant and again by the function's own first check -- and it opens only while no active SYSTEM_ADMIN exists. Day zero is reached here by revoking every active SYSTEM_ADMIN through the guard's ordinary revocation path, not by disabling anything. The operator then binds exactly ONE global assignment to an identity Supabase Auth already created; the function creates no identity of its own and refuses when none exists. It is audited under its own action name, it refuses every call after the first, and the session marker it uses is not a key on its own -- setting it by hand while an administrator exists changes nothing. ORDINARY INV-16 IS UNCHANGED: an unmarked unauthenticated grant is still refused, the bootstrapped administrator still may not grant themselves, an institution administrator still may not grant SYSTEM_ADMIN, and that administrator governs the next grant through grant_role like anybody else. AND INITIALISATION IS NOT RECOVERY: success now writes a durable record in platform_bootstrap, and that record -- not the existence of a living administrator -- is what closes the door. Revoking every SYSTEM_ADMIN in the installation does not reopen it, the record refuses UPDATE and DELETE by trigger, and the guard's day-zero clause requires the installation to be uninitialised as well as administrator-less.

A person with no past can be given their first role. The only role-granting surface built its list of people from enrolments, transfers and existing role assignments -- three prior relationships -- so the person who most needs a role, a school's first administrator created moments earlier in Supabase Auth, could not be selected at all, even though grant_role permits the grant and person_visible_to_me already returns true for them to a SYSTEM_ADMIN. persons_awaiting_first_role is the complement of those three sources and nothing wider: a person appears only while they hold no active role, no enrolment and no transfer, and leaves the list the moment they hold any of them, so the union is total and neither half is a directory. It is asserted here that the fresh person is reachable through none of the three sources, that the SYSTEM_ADMIN is offered them by name, that nobody already affiliated appears, that the grant the list exists for is accepted at the institution root, that ordinary onboarding continues from it -- the new administrator builds their own cohort -- and that an institution administrator, a dean, an educator and an anonymous caller are each refused by the SYSTEM_ADMIN name. Visibility was not widened to do any of it: the read defers to person_visible_to_me, and that predicate knows nothing about this list.

D-093 T1 (owner ruling 3 Oct, O4): an operational state has one path. A teacher who may assign cannot move or close an assessment window, end a lesson window or insert an assignment by writing the table; a school's administrator cannot change the school's own is_synthetic (which decides whether its evidence is OFFICIAL) or is_active, or write classes.status -- each refused by privilege (42501), not filtered to zero rows. Reads are unchanged; assign_release and launch_quick_assessment stay definer functions a teacher may call; service_role cannot change the installation's posture; the deployment system's change of posture is audited once, from and to, and an unchanged save is not. D-093 T2 (D-097): an operational change says what it was. A role revocation and a structure deactivation are refused without a reason; given one, each is on the record once with its previous and new state, the reason and the role the administrator acted under; the assignment keeps why it was revoked; the deactivation names every place it closed; a revoked role is not revoked twice. A seq conflict and a closed session are told apart by code. The player could not distinguish 'this client_seq is taken, renumber' from 'this session is over', so it either held an answer forever or dropped it. A different answer at a taken client_seq now raises PR001 whose DETAIL is the server's high-water mark for that item, an identical replay is acknowledged, a renumbered answer above the mark is accepted, and an answer into someone else's session raises PR002, the terminal code the player stops on.

Finish declares what the learner gave and the server holds it or refuses. A finish that raced the outbox scored the paper without the answers still travelling. finish_my_session(session, manifest) raises PR006 naming exactly the items whose declared client_seq the server does not yet hold, a seq above the held one is pending too, a malformed manifest is refused, and none of these refusals scores anything; once the answer arrives the same finish succeeds, a repeat returns the same result row, and afterwards an answer and another learner's finish each raise PR002.

An expired session waits out its late-sync window. An answer given before the deadline and received inside late_sync_grace_seconds is scorable (doc 04 §3), so the paper may not be scored the moment the clock runs out: finalize_session raises PR007 while the window is open, a finish without a manifest raises PR007, the transaction-local verified-manifest marker opens only the session it names, an answer held in another session does not satisfy the manifest, and the learner's own satisfied manifest closes the window with both the live and the late answer counted.

A sign-up creates nobody (F-02). Once an installation has an active SYSTEM_ADMIN and no fixtures marker, handle_new_auth_user refuses with PR010 a bare sign-up, a sign-up that wrote a provisioning marker into user_metadata (writable by the signer), an identity naming a person in app_metadata at insert (GoTrue writes the caller's app_metadata only after the insert, so nothing there is a key), an expired activation grant, and the synthetic seed intent on production. What is honoured is a live activation grant, consumed exactly once by an insert shaped as GoTrue makes it (app_metadata carrying only provider/providers, the address in another case), yielding the granted person and not a name the signer chose. The decision is fail-closed (`is not true`); the NULL case this session cannot reproduce is F09-C01's.

A provisioned person can be activated and signs in as themselves (F-01). persons_awaiting_account offers the school's administrator the provisioned person and nobody who already holds an account; another school's administrator, an educator and an anonymous caller are refused, as are an unknown account kind, a malformed email, a card account without a ten-digit card, a card number on an email account, and an institution administrator calling authorize_new_person. The authorized activation is audited once and writes a single-use activation grant; the identity Auth then inserts -- with nothing PINTAR wrote in app_metadata -- is linked through that grant to the provisioned person and activates their PENDING enrolment; current_person_id is that person; the person leaves the list; a second activation is refused; a SYSTEM_ADMIN may authorize a person no institution has provisioned. The same path through the real route and the real Auth service is F09-C02's. D-093 T3: an authorization alone leaves no record that an account was activated; when Auth creates the account, one account.activated row names the person, who authorized it and the role they acted under, for a provisioned person and for a new one (plants r1-4, r1-5).

F-02 on a connection that never set anything (NEW-1). The in-suite test runs on a session that has already set app.seed_intent, where current_setting(..., true) reads ''; GoTrue's connections never set it, and for them it reads NULL, which made the refusal's condition NULL and admitted every real sign-up. On fresh psql connections that never touch the setting -- asserted to read NULL -- with an active SYSTEM_ADMIN and the fixtures marker off, a sign-up shaped exactly as GoTrue inserts it (app_metadata carrying only provider/providers) is refused with PR010, and the same shape is admitted and linked to the granted person when a live activation grant names the address. Account activation through the real route and the real Auth service (NEW-2). The database suite proved activation with a hand-built auth.users insert, a shape GoTrue never produces, and passed while the product could activate nobody: GoTrue's admin createUser INSERTs the user and writes the caller's app_metadata in a later update, so the trigger never saw the link. Here a signed-in institution administrator activates a provisioned learner by classroom card and a provisioned teacher by email through POST /api/akun/aktivasi, with the fixtures marker off, and the real GoTrue creates both identities. A declared exception to the app runner's black-box rule: the world is built, and the outcome read back, through the database owner, because a provisioned person with no account is a state no seed holds; the act under test is black-box end to end.

Read: a known code wins, else its status (401 non-match, 429 rate limit, 403 refused, 503 unavailable, anything else 'could not reach PINTAR'); a wait is the route's own (the body's tunggu, else Retry-After), never invented and never outside 1..3600 s, and only on the two waits; a reference must be six capitals or digits; a destination must be inside PINTAR (no //, no other scheme); nothing else the route sends (message, error) is kept. Words, both languages: a non-match is exactly auth.card_failed ('Belum cocok'); a cooldown and a rate limit say wait and try again with the route's wait in the reader's units when given ('Tunggu 30 detik, lalu coba lagi.', 'Wait 5 minutes, then try again.') and 'sebentar' when not, and never that the card does not match (the non-match sentence is the control); a cooldown adds who to ask about a forgotten PIN; an outage gives its reference only when it has one; nothing names a code, a status or the machinery; only the two waits are drawn as a note. Screen: the card form is posted as it is to /masuk/kartu by the one fetch, the page leaves only for a signed-in answer's destination, the result is said in the one card message, signInWithCard is no longer called and the card path reads no .message/.error/.details. BOB-12's route is on the head (31c576d): the screen reads the route's own published codes (src/lib/kartu-kontrak.ts, STATUS_KARTU) rather than a copy; the route's decision (src/lib/kartu-masuk.ts) answers exactly those five; each has a sentence of its own in both languages, never the 'could not reach PINTAR' kept for an answer outside the contract; and the form and the route agree on the fields kartu, pin and lanjut. The health card counts the card's door: Konfigurasi's two public-surface checks (config.kesehatan.cek.anon_public_surface, .anon_reachable_http_paths; BOB-12's declaration, the words confirmed and the second replaced by DAISY-13) say the counts src/lib/kesehatan-skema.json expects, in both languages, and the addresses sentence names every surface the surface sentence names; a planted sentence one short is caught.

A job that never got a runner (no runner, no step) counts as queue time and costs nothing: the 5 Oct shape, 26 minutes queued, is 0 billable where the old measure said 26. A job that ran counts its runner minutes, rounded up per job for the estimate, and its wait as queue; a cancelled job that had started counts as cancelled after start; a skipped job counts for nothing. The waste alarm is red at 10 jobs that never got a runner after waiting over 5 minutes (not at 9), while 17 jobs a newer run superseded before a runner (0.6 minutes, no cost) are counted apart and are not waste, at a 16-minute wait, at a third attempt and at one commit run twice, even when it costs nothing, and not for a superseded (cancelled) run; the cost alarm is red only over the budget; the report gives compute, queue and the estimate apart.

The CI efficiency gate (D-119), that neither guard can make CI falsely green or falsely proven: executes audit/ci/proof-reuse.mjs's sameCode, DIFF_ARGS, reusable and starved, and reads the module and .github/workflows/ci.yml (selftest/ciwaste.test.ts). Only inert documents in docs/coordination, docs/reports and docs/deployment, and the staging request files, count as the same code; a code file there (.mts, .mjs, .ts, .json) never does, because tsconfig compiles every **/*.mts and lint reads every script; changed paths are listed with --no-renames, so a rename counts as both paths. Reuse needs a successful run on a branch, started by a push or a dispatch so that it tested its own head, whose strict selftest ran and succeeded, at most 72 hours old: never on main, never a pull request run (it tests a merge) or a run of unknown event, never a failed, cancelled or skipped-proof run, never a commit outside the history or a code change. A queued job of another run over 10 minutes old is starvation; a younger or running one is not. DEFERRED (starved) and ALREADY PROVEN both cancel the run, and a cancellation that does not take hold ends in exit 1, so neither is ever success. No file CI executes reads an unread path outside a comment. ci.yml runs the guard first (able to cancel its run), gates migrations and red cases on lint, typecheck and build, caps red cases at 15, supersedes per branch, filters exactly the inert unread documents, and ends in a verdict that needs every job and fails unless each succeeded.

S4 (D-091(e), approved by the owner 6 Oct as QN7): the database red cases share one local stack per group without losing a case or its isolation, read in .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/actions/local-stack/action.yml, .github/actions/local-stack/fingerprint.sql and selftest/plants/plants.json (selftest/ciwaste.test.ts). The red-case matrix holds exactly the 30 cases of 6 Oct, each in one group, and every plant gate in plants.json is one of them; every case has its steps and every step's case is in the matrix; each case's steps are contiguous, so no other case's stack step (and its reset) falls between a case's reset and its plants; each step runs on !cancelled(), so a failed case never skips a later case in its group; db-table-without-rls, which plants a migration, is alone, and a shared group holds database cases only; the defects are injected per case of the group. The local-stack action boots only when no stack runs, resets the database on every use, and fails the use when the fresh database's fingerprint (functions, column and relation grants, policies, triggers, extensions, roles, memberships, role settings, row counts) differs from the job's first; the fingerprint only reads.

The public-repository guard (Batch 0 B0-C; D-143): executes scripts/guard/sensitive-scan.mjs on planted text built at run time (selftest/secguard.test.ts). Refused, by fingerprint only: a private-key header; GitHub, AWS, Supabase, Stripe, Slack, Google, Resend and npm tokens; a JWT granting service_role from a real project; a database URL with a password on a real host; a secret assigned in an env file; a credential inside a synthetic fixture directory (never allowed by path); a personal address; a plausible NIK; an undeclared answer-key package, including one under audit/fixtures; and, since F-4 (D-145(b)), keyed content in any text file (class kunci-jawaban): three or more is_correct-true markers in JSON, TypeScript, SQL or Markdown that is not a package (a fixture directory too), a generator's keyed option tuples (Python and JS; a reason opening Benar or Tepat), a misconception CSV whose header has both code and questions. Allowed: the local stack's demo JWT, synthetic and reserved domains, organisational role addresses, stand-in tokens, a localhost database URL, an environment or workflow secret reference, a declared synthetic package, code, a test or a migration that merely mentions is_correct (at most twice in a file), the same keyed content in a file declared sintetis, a CSV with a code column and no question map, and a tuple whose reason is neither «Benar» nor «Tepat». No finding carries the matched value.
